prompt: A damaged barcode scans successfully on each attempt with probability $0.3$, independently. What is the probability that it takes MORE than $3$ attempts to get the first successful scan? Round to three decimal places.
hint: Think about what "more than $3$ attempts" says about the first three attempts. Nothing after them matters.

hints.text: Think about what "more than $3$ attempts" says about the first three attempts. Nothing after them matters.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: "more than 1 attempt" just means the first attempt failed: probability $0.7$. "More than 2" means the first two failed: $0.7^2 = 0.49$. Keep going.
The first three attempts must all fail, and each fails with probability $0.7$. So $P(Y > 3) = (1 - p)^3 = (0.7)^3$.
$(0.7)^3 = 0.343$, so the probability that it takes more than $3$ attempts is $0.343$.

explanation: Let $Y$ be the attempt on which the first success occurs, so $Y$ is geometric with $p = 0.3$.
$Y > 3$ happens exactly when attempts 1, 2 and 3 all fail, and by independence $P(Y > 3) = 0.7 \times 0.7 \times 0.7$.
$0.7^3 = 0.343$, so the probability of needing more than three attempts is $0.343$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add up the first three and subtract
steps: $P(Y > 3) = 1 - 0.657 = 0.343$. Same answer, more work — the "all failures" shortcut is faster.
